I have been farming these 3 mu in Quzhou for 18 years, so I know what works on my land. With only 3 mu and some family members working off-farm, I cannot take big risks or try fancy new methods. I need reliable crops that fit the local wheat-maize rotation and a small cotton patch for cash.

This year I will keep my usual split: **2 mu for the wheat-maize rotation** and **1 mu for cotton**. The wheat-maize system feeds my family and gives steady grain income, while cotton brings in cash. I have a well, so water is not my biggest worry, though I watch the electricity cost for the pump.

For **winter wheat** on the 2 mu, I will use rotary tillage before sowing—this is what everyone in my village does. I will plant an improved variety like the ones my neighbors use; they are reliable and yield well here. I will put down compound fertilizer as a base and top-dress with urea, which comes to about 17 kg of nitrogen, 9 kg of phosphorus, and 5.5 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times: once before winter, once at jointing, and once during grain filling. Wheat also needs some spraying, so I will apply pesticide about four times in total for weeds, insects, and disease. If the weather is normal, I expect around 540 kg per mu.

For **summer maize** on the same 2 mu, there is no time to plough after wheat harvest, so I will direct-seed with no-tillage. I will use a hybrid maize seed—hybrids grow fast and give good yields. Fertilizer will be about 11 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu, again using compound fertilizer and a urea top-dressing. Maize does not need as much water as wheat, so I will irrigate twice, mainly during the critical flowering and grain-filling stages. I will spray pesticide three times. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

For **cotton** on the remaining 1 mu, I will rotary till the soil in spring and plant a hybrid cotton variety. Cotton needs more care than grain crops, especially pest control, so I will spray pesticide about twelve times through the season to fight bollworms and aphids. I will apply roughly 7.5 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium per mu, using compound fertilizer. I will irrigate twice—once at flowering and once during the boll stage. I hope for about 240 kg of seed cotton per mu, which is a decent yield for my village.

decision.reasoning_summary: With 3 mu of land and some family members working off-farm, I split my field into 2 mu for the reliable wheat-maize rotation and 1 mu for cotton cash income. I use well irrigation, rotary tillage for wheat and cotton, and no-tillage for summer maize to save time. I apply moderate fertilizer rates using compound fertilizer and urea, irrigate according to each crop's needs, and spray pesticides intensively on cotton because bollworms are a constant threat. These practices match what other middle-educated women farmers in Quzhou with similar small farms do, and they give steady yields without requiring more labor than I can manage.
